title: Enterprise decision heuristics for model fallbacks and sourcing latency buckets
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Objective: produce a pragmatic, operational decision heuristic that guides engineering and sales teams on which model variants and procurement pathways to use based on region, observed latency buckets, cost deltas, and substitutability evidence. This should translate market research and competitive signals into concrete provisioning triggers and monitoring alerts that scale across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Background: customers increasingly ask for explicit fallback rules when primary model supply degrades or becomes cost-inefficient in a region. We have scattered heuristics (notes in Confluence) and several ad-hoc dashboards; we lack a single decision artifact that (a) sales/solutions can reference in SOW discussions, (b) runtime can consume for routing defaults, and (c) PM/analytics can use to evaluate model switch impact on latency and unit economics.

Scope & deliverables (MVP):
- Decision Heuristic Matrix CSV: rows = {region, customer_tier, latency_bucket, cost_delta_pct, substitutability_score_threshold, recommended_action}. Latency buckets: <50ms, 50-150ms, >150ms (client-facing).
- Playbook doc (Confluence): step-by-step procurement and canary rollout instructions for each heuristic row plus owner checklist. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Model+Fallback+Heuristics (MVP page).
- Dashboard prototype: a single view with regional latency distribution, model availability, cost delta heatmap, and a list of triggered heuristics. Link: https://app.redwood.ai/dashboards/model-supply (proto).
- API spec snippet for routing defaults that runtime will accept (RFC to ENG).
- One customer-facing FAQ paragraph and internal sales brief summarizing expected latency/cost tradeoffs.

Methodology:
1) Competitive scan: collect recent public outages/capacity alerts from major model vendors and cloud providers (last 12 months) and translate them to observed latency/capacity signals.
2) Synthetic benchmarking: run synthetic RAG+chat workloads across representative regions to measure P50/P95 latency for top 6 open models and our Redwood-verified variants; derive cost-per-token deltas at typical batch sizes.
3) Substitutability scoring: combine output-quality regression checks (evalsets), architectural compatibility (quantization/kompat), and community adoption signals into a 0-100 score.
4) Economics thresholds: propose cost_delta_pct thresholds that justify auto-fallback vs. human review (initial suggestion: auto-fallback if cost_delta >= 30% AND substitutability_score >= 75 AND latency bucket <= 150ms).

Acceptance criteria:
- Heuristic matrix in CSV populated for top 8 regions and three customer tiers (SMB, Midmarket, Enterprise).
- Playbook doc reviewed and approved by Solutions Engineering and Runtime leads (approvals recorded in comments).
- Dashboard prototype populates live metrics and demonstrates at least two triggered heuristic examples in staging.
- RFC sent to ENG with sample JSON payload and at least one follow-up sync scheduled.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Aggressive auto-fallbacks reduce latency incidents but increase switching churn and potential quality regressions. We'll bias safety for Enterprise tiers (require higher substitutability).
- Using coarse latency buckets simplifies decisioning but may miss transient spikes; mitigation: require sustained signal for >2 minutes before auto-fallback.
